### Day 60: 2 Samuel 12:24–25
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-60-2-samuel-12-2425.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 12:24-25
Points:
- God is not detached from human sorrow but deeply feels and responds to the cries of His people.
- The painful loss forced David out of self-sufficiency back into humble dependence on God.
- Restored intimacy with the Lord empowered David to comfort his grieving wife and return to worship.
- In gracious mercy, God blessed the union of David and Bathsheba with Solomon, naming him beloved.
- While God’s discipline can be severe, He never abandons His children and continually seeks their restoration.

### Riding Out the Storm
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/individual/riding-out-the-storm
Passage: 2 Samuel 12:24
Points:
- After severe consequences, David refused to surrender to despair and instead comforted his grieving wife.
- Recovering from crisis requires moving past self-pity and choosing to resume life with renewed purpose.
- Navigating the storm involves praying, accepting reality, and placing full trust in God's sovereignty.
- Facing the lonely aftermath of tragedy is painful, but the whirlwind is only temporary.
- Believers enduring difficult seasons must persevere by relying on God for daily strength.
